question: Allocation by the Commission of an additional EUR 3 billion to EU Member States providing assistance to Ukrainian nationals since 2022

On 26 August 2025, during a conversation with journalists in Brussels, Commission spokesperson Markus Lammert said that under the Temporary Protection Directive of March 2022 (extended in August this year until March 2027), EU Member States are obliged to provide the necessary social security, health care and means of subsistence for those who do not have sufficient funds themselves1.

In May, the Commission published a decision to allocate an additional EUR 3 billion to Member States hosting Ukrainian refugees2. In light of the above: Which Member States have received financial support from the Commission from the start of the war in Ukraine until today, in what amounts and for which specific programmes?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.12.2025) The implementation of the programming period 2014-2020 of the Home Affairs Funds1 was extended by one year to allow Member States to use the remaining funds to address the challenges resulting from Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

During the programming period 2021–2027, EUR 385 million were allocated as emergency assistance in 2022 from the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF)2 and the Border Management and Visa Instrument3 to the Member States most affected by the mass influx of displaced persons from Ukraine4. EUR 7 million were earmarked for the 'Safe homes' initiative5. In 2023, EUR 8 million were earmarked for a EUR 31.

2 million International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)-led project, offering psychological first aid and psychosocial support in 28 countries6. EUR 65.2 million were allocated under an AMIF Specific Action to Bulgaria, Czechia, Poland, and Romania for hosting a high number of beneficiaries of temporary protection. Currently, EUR 1.

5 billion is being made available under AMIF to support Member States with the implementation of the Pact on Migration and Asylum and for hosting displaced persons from Ukraine. Under the 2021-2027 cohesion funds, EUR 1.
